items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: That night, I went quite early to the Savoy because I did not want to miss a note coming from the horn of Satchel. ... When Satchelmouth came on the stand I was pleasantly surprised because he was a much better looking man than the few bad photos I had seen and collected of him.

ctx.x: Tabbs had the best hominy grits, sausages and eggs with hot biscuits and butter oozing from them, that you ever stuck a tooth in. And thats what I decided to have after I left Bobby to feed some of the juice that I had drunk at his uncle's place. Bobby Starke and I became very good friends.

I dont remember who was in Lou Russell's band when they played at the Savoy on Easter Monday 1929 with us and the Royal Flush orchestra of Fess Williams but he was advertised to play two nights with Louis Armstrong. Russell's first name was Luis but the Savoy had him billed as Lou. Armstrong was being called Satchelmouth now and this was the first time he was coming to New York since he had left Fletcher Henderson. I was still in Cincinnati when that happened and as Armstrong was not with Fletcher when he came to…

of being able to see and hear my idol for the first time. That night, I went quite early to the Savoy because I did not want to miss a note coming from the horn of Satchel. There was a trumpet player with him whom I had met named Louis Metcalf. Metcalf sat on a high stool, wore a cardboard gold crown and called himself 'King Louis'!
